name: Leaf Rust
cause: Fungal spores carried on wind during humid, mild weather (15–22°C). Common in wheat and barley during early spring.
symptoms: Orange-brown pustules on the upper leaf surface
Pustules rub off as rusty powder when touched
Leaves yellow and dry up prematurely
chemicalTreatment: Propiconazole 25% EC at 0.1% — one spray at first symptoms
Tebuconazole 250 EC at 1 ml/L if infection advances
Repeat after 10–12 days if rain continues
organicTreatment: Cow urine 1:10 with water as foliar spray
Trichoderma viride soil drench at tillering
prevention: Rotate with non-cereal crops every 2 seasons
Remove volunteer wheat plants between seasons

name: Black Spot
cause: Fungal pathogen spread through warm, wet conditions and overhead watering. Common on rose, tomato and brinjal.
symptoms: Dark circular spots on leaves with concentric rings
Yellow halos surrounding the spots
Premature defoliation
chemicalTreatment: Mancozeb 75% WP at 2 g/L — two sprays 10 days apart
Chlorothalonil at 2.5 g/L for persistent infections
organicTreatment: Baking soda solution (1 tsp per litre) weekly
Neem oil 2% spray on infected plants
prevention: Water at the base, avoid wetting leaves
Ensure 60cm spacing between plants for air flow

name: Powdery Mildew
cause: Fungal infection that thrives in warm days (20–27°C) and cool, humid nights. Common on cucurbits, grapes and peas.
symptoms: White powdery coating on upper leaf surface
Leaves curl and become brittle
Stunted growth in severe cases
chemicalTreatment: Sulphur dust 20 kg/ha in early morning

name: Early Blight
cause: Soil-borne fungus activated by warm humid weather. Affects potato, tomato and other Solanaceae.
symptoms: Dark concentric lesions starting on lower leaves
Yellowing spreads upward through plant
Stem cankers in severe cases
organicTreatment: Compost tea soil drench every 10 days
Neem cake in soil before sowing
prevention: Rotate crops — avoid Solanaceae for 3 years
Stake plants so leaves don't touch soil

name: Late Blight
cause: Oomycete pathogen spreading rapidly in cool (10–20°C) wet weather. Caused the Irish potato famine.
symptoms: Water-soaked grey-green spots on leaves
White downy mould on underside in humid weather
Rapid collapse of entire plants within days
chemicalTreatment: Remove and bury affected plants immediately
organicTreatment: Limit irrigation during cool damp spells

name: Mosaic Virus
scientificName: Tobacco Mosaic Virus / Cucumber Mosaic Virus
cause: Viral infection transmitted by aphids and through contaminated tools. No cure once infected — management focuses on prevention.
symptoms: Mottled light and dark green pattern on leaves
Leaves curl, crinkle and become leathery
Stunted plants with reduced yield
chemicalTreatment: No chemical cure — control aphid vectors with Imidacloprid 0.3 ml/L
Remove and burn infected plants immediately
Disinfect tools with 10% bleach between plants
organicTreatment: Neem oil to suppress aphid populations

name: Anthracnose
cause: Fungal infection triggered by warm (24–28°C) wet weather. Affects beans, mango, grape, chilli.
symptoms: Sunken dark spots on fruit and pods
Pink spore masses in centre of lesions
Wilting of young shoots
organicTreatment: Trichoderma spray — foliar and soil drench

name: Downy Mildew
cause: Oomycete spreading in cool (15–23°C) humid weather. Common on grapes, cucurbits and spinach.
symptoms: Yellow angular patches on upper leaf surface
Greyish-purple fuzzy growth on underside
Leaves shrivel and drop
chemicalTreatment: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb 2.5 g/L at first sign

name: Bacterial Wilt
cause: Soil-borne bacteria that enter through root wounds in warm, waterlogged conditions. No chemical cure.
symptoms: Sudden wilting despite moist soil
White milky ooze from cut stems in water
Yellowing and plant death within a week
chemicalTreatment: No effective chemical — focus on crop rotation
Copper oxychloride soil drench as preventive
Bleaching powder 15 kg/ha for soil sterilisation

name: Fusarium Wilt
cause: Persistent soil fungus entering through roots. Survives in soil for many years. Common on tomato, banana, cotton.
symptoms: One-sided yellowing and wilting of leaves
Brown streaks in vascular tissue when stem is cut
Entire plant collapses eventually
organicTreatment: Trichoderma viride at sowing and transplanting
prevention: Avoid replanting same family in same plot

name: Leaf Curl
cause: Virus transmitted by whiteflies. Affects tomato, chilli, cotton.
symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of leaves
Yellowing between veins
Stunted growth and no fruit set
organicTreatment: Neem oil 5% spray on undersides of leaves
Reflective silver mulch to repel whitefly

name: Sheath Blight
cause: Fungal disease of rice. Favoured by high nitrogen, dense canopy, and warm humid nights.
symptoms: Oval lesions on sheath near water line
Lesions expand with grey centres and brown borders
Tiller death in severe cases

name: Tikka Leaf Spot
cause: Fungal leaf spot on groundnut, spread by wind and rain in warm humid weather.
symptoms: Circular brown spots with yellow halo
Defoliation in severe infections
Reduced pod filling

name: Stem Rust
cause: Wind-borne fungal spores. Major wheat pathogen. Warm (20–25°C) humid weather triggers outbreaks.
symptoms: Reddish-brown pustules on stems and leaf sheaths
Stems break or lodge in severe cases
Shrivelled grain
chemicalTreatment: Two sprays 10 days apart if rain continues

name: Root Rot
cause: Multiple soil fungi that attack roots in waterlogged, compacted soils.
symptoms: Stunted growth and yellowing
Roots turn dark, soft and mushy
Easy to pull plant out of soil
